description: STRING THEORY — a Karplus-Strong plucked string: a burst of noise or external audio is fed into a short delay line and recirculated, and the length of that line sets the pitch.

params.text: Sets the length of the delay line, 1ms to 500ms, which is the coarse pitch of the string. A patched voltage adds a tenth of the range per volt.
Adds up to 20ms to the length of the delay line. A patched voltage adds 1ms per volt.
Adds up to 200 further samples to the length of the delay line, for tuning finer than the time knobs reach. A patched voltage adds 20 samples per volt.
Sets how much of the string is fed back into itself, from full inversion through silence to full, so the string rings on or dies away. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Feeds the output of each string into another string rather than back into itself, stepping by up to 8 strings. A patched voltage adds a step per 10V.
Tones the strings: below halfway a lowpass closes toward 20Hz, above halfway a highpass rises toward 20kHz, and the centre leaves them unfiltered. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Plucks the strings, sending a burst of noise or of the external input into each delay line; the button and a rising edge at the jack both do it.
Steps through the three noise sources used for the pluck and the ring modulator: white, pink and Gaussian.
Sets how many strings are plucked at once, 1 to 8.
Delays the start of each successive string by a share of the delay time, 0 to 100%, so they are plucked in turn rather than together. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Stretches the burst going into each successive string, 0 to 100%, which detunes them from one another. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Sets how many of the strings are ring modulated, counting from the first, up to 8. A patched voltage adds a step per 10V.
Blends each ring modulated string between its plain and ring modulated form, 0 to 100%. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Steps through three shapes for the burst going into the strings: unlit is none, green is a Hanning window, blue is a Blackman window.
Steps through four ways of limiting the feedback: unlit is off, red clips, yellow compresses at 20 to 1, green compresses adaptively.

inputs.text: Sets the length of the delay line, 1ms to 500ms, which is the coarse pitch of the string. A patched voltage adds a tenth of the range per volt.
Adds up to 20ms to the length of the delay line. A patched voltage adds 1ms per volt.
Adds up to 200 further samples to the length of the delay line, for tuning finer than the time knobs reach. A patched voltage adds 20 samples per volt.
Sets the pitch of the strings, tracking a volt per octave, by dividing the delay line length.
Sets how much of the string is fed back into itself, from full inversion through silence to full, so the string rings on or dies away. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Feeds the output of each string into another string rather than back into itself, stepping by up to 8 strings. A patched voltage adds a step per 10V.
Tones the strings: below halfway a lowpass closes toward 20Hz, above halfway a highpass rises toward 20kHz, and the centre leaves them unfiltered. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Audio patched here is used for the pluck burst in place of the internal noise.
Plucks the strings, sending a burst of noise or of the external input into each delay line; the button and a rising edge at the jack both do it.
A polyphonic signal patched here replaces the strings in the feedback path, one channel per string.
Stretches the burst going into each successive string, 0 to 100%, which detunes them from one another. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Delays the start of each successive string by a share of the delay time, 0 to 100%, so they are plucked in turn rather than together. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Sets how many of the strings are ring modulated, counting from the first, up to 8. A patched voltage adds a step per 10V.
Blends each ring modulated string between its plain and ring modulated form, 0 to 100%. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Audio patched here is used as the ring modulator's carrier in place of the internal noise.

outputs.text: Carries the sum of the strings, scaled down by the square root of their number.
Carries the strings before their filtering, one polyphonic channel per string, so effects can be placed in the feedback path.

notes: silent until the PLUCK button is pressed or a trigger arrives at the pluck input; each pluck is what feeds a burst into the delay lines.

inputs.3: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.8: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
